questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an english speaking country where there also was interesting courses. Furthermore, the beautiful nature and scottish culture was the reason why I chose Scotland.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many of the courses I wanted where not available for exchange student (limited class number), so my courses were not as great as I had hoped for.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. St. Andrews has a Global Office responsible for their exchange students. They are good at sending out information and if you have any further questions, you can always email them and they are are happy to help + fast at responding.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Global Office are very easy to contact and visible during orientation week. Additionally, during the first day there is Academic adivising where you talk through your module choices which is also very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: St. Andrews offers halls to first year students and visting students. There are different types of halls and rooms, but they generally offer catered and non-catered options and then you can chose if you want to have your own room or share a room, and whether or not you want your own bathroom.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You can chose to be catered, where you get meals served or be non-catered where you cook your own food. All halls have shared kitchens so if you can always cook your own food, even if you are catered.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very fun! But it is primarily first year students that live there. There are a lot of options, but the biggest hall is called David Russel Apartments and a lot of exchange students end up there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Chosing a catered option is a great way to meet people in the beginning, but the food is not great and you will probably get tired of it after a couple of months.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Berfore coming to St. Andrews you have to complete pre-advising, where you also choose provisional modules. Then when you arrive at St. Andrews you have a meeting with an academic adviser to finalise your modules.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get assigned an academic adviser, but the Global Office is also always availible. Additionally, during the first week of teaching you are able to change your modules, if they are not what you expected.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Semi-succesful. I got 2/4 modules I wanted, but there were not very many alternatives available to me, but it all depends on availability for the given modules, your interests and the schedules. I think I was just a bit unlucky, because many others I talked to were very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient. The registration is at the orientation week, so you need to wait until then to get your modules.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I primarily took 4th year courses, but had one 2nd year course as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are more presentations, assignments, quizzes and generally participation during the semester. These are typically graded and count towards your final grade, but it means that the exams count less.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Research Methods in Biology (BL2300), Antimicrobials - Mode of Action and Resistance (BL4211), Structure-based Drug Discovery (BL4216) and Advanced Microscopy and Image Analysis - Seeing is Believing (BL4225),

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Structure-based Drug Discovery. It is a project-oriented course, where you work in groups. It is very interesting and different from any courses I have tried at UCPH.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: We did not need any books. All of my books were provided as online copies to the students, so I did not have to buy any books.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are too many to list, all from sports to book clubs and communities. During the first week there is an activity fair, where all sports and societies are represented.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was a part of the knitting society. That was very low-key and a great way to meet and talk to people in a relaxed setting.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Scotland! It can be a bit difficult to get to and from St. Andrews, but there are many busses, so it just requires a little planning. Otherwise there are a great deal of pubs, that can be very fun during weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. St. Andrews is a University town so it is very young and vibrant.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies. Many of the local students take part in societies and sports, so that is a great way to get to know them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It might not be as much of a cultural difference, but I had a hard time adjusting to the teaching style and academics.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were super friendly!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about coursework, join a society and take a trip to the highlands at least once.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: St. Andrews is a very international university, so there were not as many scottish people as I expected, but instead people from all around the world, which was great!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The independence and the new international community you got to be a part of.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to a completely different system and school.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
